text: Use /init to create concise, repository-backed AGENTS.md guidance.
Use /profile to select plan, orchestrator, debug, ask, or code.
Alt+A cycles profiles by default; customize app.profile.cycle in keybindings.json.
Use /setup-agents to choose per-profile models; /setup-agents defaults fills missing project settings without replacing configured values.
Automatic profile routing is opt-in with tark.auto_profile in settings.json. Manual profile selection pins it; /profile auto resumes routing when enabled.
Auto plan: start with plan, design, outline, analyze, think through, approach, let's plan, help me plan, make a plan, or create a plan.
Auto debug: start with debug, investigate, fix, error, bug, broken, failing, crash, or failure. You can prefix these with help me.
Auto orchestrator: start with orchestrate, coordinate, delegate, parallelize, split into tasks, split this into tasks, split it into tasks, or use subagents.
Auto code: start with create, make, add, implement, build, write, execute, generate, edit, modify, update, remove, delete, or refactor.
Auto ask: start with explain, answer, tell me, clarify, what, how, why, where, when, or who.
Auto routing matches request openings, ignoring case and polite prefixes like please or can you. Unmatched or conflicting requests keep the current profile.
After planning, say Implement the plan for code or Delegate the plan to subagents for orchestrator. Go ahead, proceed, and continue do not switch profiles.
Give subagents self-contained tasks and precise write paths; they do not inherit the conversation.
Read-only exploration is always available: ask with purpose explore uses small_model when configured, otherwise the current model.
Subagent scopes coordinate shared-workspace writes; they are not a security sandbox.
Use the diagnosing-bugs skill to establish evidence before changing code.
Use code-review for correctness review, or safe-refactor for behavior-preserving changes.
Use tdd for test-first development and verify-and-stop to check acceptance criteria.
Use ponytail for the smallest complete change, keeping validation and required tests.
Name relevant files, constraints, and acceptance criteria so the agent knows when to stop.
Use grilling to clarify important unknowns without turning clear tasks into interviews.
UI/UX searches require Python 3; agent-browser requires its CLI and browser binaries separately.
Use /summary for work, decisions, open questions, and next steps.
Use /commit to draft a commit message; it does not commit files.
Use /repo-cache-status for local outline-cache hits, misses, and size.
Repository indexes contain declaration snippets; treat ~/.tark/cache as private source-derived data.
askquestions supports choices, multiple selections, and text; cancellation is not consent.
Tab revisits related questions by default without losing drafts.
Use /sound to configure tark.sound in ~/.tark/settings.json; provide attention.wav, finished.wav, and failure.wav in ~/.tark/sounds/.
Context warnings start at 50%, errors at 80%; cost is an estimate, not a provider invoice.
Footer token and cost totals include all session branches and subagent results.
Use /reload after changing configuration or resources; choose orange or midnight in /settings.
